intro:
Binh Gia and the coastal approaches — 28 December 1964

Fighting around Binh Gia is drawing South Vietnamese troops into the countryside east of Saigon. Before they can concentrate, our coastal detachments have a chance to strike the positions at Long Hai and Vung Tau.

Take those bases and break the defensive network around them. Local forces know the approach routes, but government reserves can return along the roads behind us. Make the enemy answer our attack without leaving the detachments cut off on the coast.

intro:
Escape from Vung Tau — 29 December 1964

The raid on the coast has brought a response. South Vietnamese troops are moving to seal the roads around Vung Tau, and our detachments must reach the jungle routes before the cordon closes.

Lead the withdrawal through the designated exits, with a rearguard covering the slowest groups. If the roads are blocked, hold the remaining bases together until the pressure eases. Do not let the fighting around the crash site draw the force away from its route out.

intro:
Plei Me — 19 October 1965

The camp at Plei Me watches the routes through the Central Highlands. Its locally recruited garrison and American advisers can call on aircraft and relief troops from the Pleiku area.

Attack the camp while a blocking force secures the northern road. Hold the positions you take against the relief column. The operation will fail if the two attacking groups are separated and the road to the garrison remains open.

Now you should disappear quickly into the jungle before the Americans arrive again to claim revenge!.

intro:
Ia Drang — 14 November 1965

American helicopter-borne troops are establishing landing zones near our routes through the Central Highlands. Their aircraft can bring reinforcements beyond a conventional front line, but the men on the ground still need clearings they can hold.

Drive them from X-Ray, Albany and the surrounding positions. Local detachments will support the attack. Use the jungle to approach the clearings; American artillery and aircraft can strike any assault group left in the open.

intro:
Cu Chi: preserve the local force — 4 January 1966

An enemy clearing operation is closing on Cu Chi. The local detachments know the villages and supply routes on which our work here depends. We need those people alive when the enemy columns have passed.

Cover their withdrawal towards War Zone C. Send the local groups ahead and use the stronger formations to hold the routes behind them. A defensible base can give us time, but do not let the defence of it trap the force we are trying to save.

briliant.text:
Good work. The local VC units are safe, and we took only minimal losses. The enemy thinks he has occupied the so-called ''Iron Triangle'', but many of our southern comrades are now hidden in this areas secret underground tunnels. They are preparing their former positions for the return of our troops there.

Hanoi wants to celebrate your victory by moving your troops to a quiet place to give you and your men a rest.

intro:
Tuy Hoa — 18 July 1967

South Korean troops are preparing to clear our positions around Tuy Hoa. The bases here give our local forces access to the coastal districts; losing them would leave those detachments without a secure route inland.

Hold the bases and draw exposed troops back into positions they can defend together. PAVN formations are available to strengthen the line. Keep the roads between the defenders open as the enemy advances.

intro:
Kontum outposts — 3 November 1967

Government outposts around Dak Pek, Dak Seang, Dak To and Kontum overlook the routes between our border bases and the interior. An enemy offensive is expected, and these camps would give it places to assemble and resupply.

Take the outposts and hold them. Cover the relief routes while the assault groups close on each camp; otherwise fresh troops can arrive as quickly as we drive the garrison back.

intro:
Khe Sanh — 15 January 1968

The American base at Khe Sanh watches Route 9 near the Laotian border. Its airstrip and hill positions overlook the approaches to our supply network, and aircraft can sustain the garrison even if the ground routes are cut.

Take the surrounding hills, Lang Vei and the combat base with its airstrip. Reinforcements are coming to support the attack. Bring the guns into position before exposing the assault troops: the defenders' artillery can still reach well beyond their perimeter.

intro:
Tet offensive: Hue and Da Nang — 31 January 1968

The Tet offensive is bringing the war into the cities. Our attacking groups have a brief chance to disrupt the South Vietnamese command before government and American reserves can respond.

Strike Hue and the Da Nang area. At Hue, the ARVN First Division headquarters and the American advisory compound are important centres of resistance. The rocket batteries will support the assaults; once inside the cities, hold the captured positions against the counterattack.

intro:
Laos counteroffensive — 12 February 1971

South Vietnamese forces have entered Laos along Route 9 with American air support. Their landing sites and firebases threaten the supply routes that connect our northern bases with the fighting in the south.

Drive them from the Xe Pon valley and recover Tchepone and Route 9. Take the isolated bases before helicopters can reinforce them or lift the defenders out. Our heavier weapons give the assault groups more support, but aircraft still make the open approaches dangerous.

intro:
Kontum — 15 May 1972

The offensive has returned to the Central Highlands. South Vietnamese forces hold Kontum behind a chain of firebases, with American advisers and aircraft supporting the defence.

Break the outer positions and take the city. Regional units will join the advance, and our anti-aircraft weapons can cover parts of the approach. The defenders will try to hold the assault groups under air attack before they reach the streets.

intro:
Saigon — 24 April 1975

The South Vietnamese armies have lost the northern provinces and the Central Highlands. Surviving formations are falling back towards Saigon, where the government is trying to put together another defence.

Take Bien Hoa and the capital's command and communications centres, then clear the routes towards the coast. The converging columns must reach the city before the defenders can organise a new line. A slow advance will give them time we cannot afford.

Campaign note: a Tactical Victory ends the campaign unsuccessfully; meet a higher victory deadline.
